newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's TAM seeks air cargo joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's TAM seeks air cargo joint venture.

text.p: Brazilian airline TAM said it is in talks with U.S firms Martin Air, Fast Air and Federal Express Corp in hopes of forming an air cargo partnership with one of them in Paraguay's Ciudad del Este.
Rolim Amaro, TAM's president, told reporters at a business breakfast that the company wants to enter a partnership with an experienced firm to learn how to operate in the air cargo market.
"After getting the know-how, we can decide whether or not to enter this business on our own," he said, adding TAM will provide more details on a possible deal next week.
Meanwhile, TAM has agreed to lease ten Fokker-100 passenger planes, of which five will be used in its Paraguayan unit, Lapsa, Rolim said. TAM acquired Lapsa on September 1.
"Most of these planes will be used in our existing routes to increase flights," he said.
TAM is the fatest growing regional airline in Brazil. Last year, the firm saw its net profit jump to $43.9 million from $18.1 million in 1994.
The number of passengers it transported rose 84 percent to three million last year.
